rules.source_observation: Interview guidance favors neutral prompts and concrete lived examples.
rules.decision: Anchor demand evidence on a recent problem, workaround and consequence; label hypothetical praise separately.
rules.trigger: An idea is supported mainly by compliments or an AI-generated persona.
rules.verification: A consented evidence note links each claim to an actual example, or explicitly records that interviews were not run.
rules.limits: A reported story is not audited behavior or market prevalence.

rules.source_observation: Research objectives should clarify the decision and assumptions under examination.
rules.decision: Predefine one next decision and disconfirming evidence before adding features.
rules.trigger: The product backlog grows without a testable business question.
rules.verification: Decision brief states customer, assumption, evidence needed and continue/change/stop conditions.
rules.limits: Thresholds are owner choices, not universal empirical cutoffs.

rules.source_observation: Moderated testing observes whether participants can complete defined tasks.
rules.decision: Separate problem evidence, usable interaction, willingness to commit and actual payment.
rules.trigger: A prototype demo is being described as validated demand.
rules.verification: Evidence matrix names which stage was observed and leaves other stages unknown.
rules.limits: Usability and satisfaction cannot substitute for purchase evidence.

rules.source_observation: The report samples revenue-active integrated apps rather than all attempted products.
rules.decision: Use external benchmarks to choose questions, not forecast this app or mandate a paywall.
rules.trigger: A published conversion median is being used as a guaranteed local target.
rules.verification: Cohort, denominator, period, statistic and selection limits accompany any comparison.
rules.limits: Observational association is not a causal treatment effect.

rules.source_observation: Research is organized around explicit questions and actual likely users.
rules.decision: Prefer a bounded, honestly described manual pilot when it can answer the question before automation.
rules.trigger: Automation scope exceeds the evidence that a reachable customer needs the outcome.
rules.verification: Pilot brief includes delivery effort, recruitment assumptions, consent and authorized cost.
rules.limits: Manual delivery is a proposed tactic; no simulated customer or fake purchase counts as evidence.

rules.source_observation: An alerts-only budget does not itself stop usage or billing.
rules.decision: Record separately what notifies, what rejects new work and what still accrues charges.
rules.trigger: A budget email threshold is being called a hard cap.
rules.verification: Control inventory names enforcement path and a safe dry-run rejection test.
rules.limits: Do not generalize this alert-only limitation to eligible spend-cap products.

rules.source_observation: Eligible project/service spend caps can block new work but have enforcement lag and ongoing-charge exceptions.
rules.decision: Track cap coverage, in-flight exposure and fixed costs; recheck restoration behavior before relying on it.
rules.trigger: A provider cap is presented as an immediate whole-account ceiling.
rules.verification: Budget model includes scope, billing units, latency and exclusions.
rules.limits: No provider control in this source proves zero overshoot; reset semantics were not adopted.

rules.source_observation: Supabase lists compute and several opted-in items outside Spend Cap coverage.
rules.decision: Maintain a covered-versus-excluded cost ledger instead of assuming the plan price caps the invoice.
rules.trigger: A plan cap is being used as the total infrastructure budget.
rules.verification: All active cost items have explicit coverage and evidence timestamps.
rules.limits: Coverage changes with product and plan; this is not a current invoice audit.

rules.source_observation: Resource abuse can amplify paid operations; limits include payload, batch, duration and frequency.
rules.decision: Guard expensive operations at their real cost boundary, not merely by counting outer HTTP requests.
rules.trigger: One allowed request can trigger many costly nested operations.
rules.verification: Local fixtures exercise batch, upload, retry and identity limits without calling paid providers.
rules.limits: Defensive fixture success is not a complete security audit.

rules.source_observation: Delayed enforcement and operation amplification leave residual cost exposure.
rules.decision: Reserve bounded estimated cost atomically before dispatch and reconcile actual cost after completion.
rules.trigger: Concurrent workers all observe the same remaining allowance.
rules.verification: Concurrency/crash tests show reservations cannot be double-spent or released while work remains billable.
rules.limits: An authored design pattern, not a provider guarantee; unbounded unit cost prevents a hard local ceiling claim.

rules.source_observation: Paddle documents repeated delivery, event_id identity and out-of-order arrival.
rules.decision: Deduplicate the business event and protect state ordering; transport delivery IDs alone are insufficient.
rules.trigger: A retry can grant credits again or an old event can resurrect access.
rules.verification: Duplicate and reversed-order fixtures preserve one intended business effect.
rules.limits: Credit grants need a purchase/period business key as well as event transport deduplication.

rules.source_observation: Paddle signature validation depends on the signed request content and endpoint secret.
rules.decision: Verify the untouched body before parsing into trusted domain state; persist receipt before acknowledging durable acceptance.
rules.trigger: A handler trusts JSON fields or acknowledges an event kept only in memory.
rules.verification: Tamper, wrong-secret and durable-write-failure fixtures cannot grant access or falsely accept receipt.
rules.limits: Durable inbox ordering is authored synthesis; provider signature behavior must match the deployed SDK.

rules.source_observation: Paddle recommends state-based access and periodic reconciliation; scheduled cancellation can be future-effective.
rules.decision: Model cancellation request, effective expiry and immediate revocation separately, with a repair path for drift.
rules.trigger: Cancel-click immediately removes paid-through access or missed events persist forever.
rules.verification: Future cancellation retains valid access; authoritative refresh repairs a deliberately stale local fixture.
rules.limits: Grace/hold/refund policy is provider- and product-specific, not a blanket keep-access rule.

rules.source_observation: Google Play requires verified purchase eligibility and distinguishes PURCHASED from PENDING.
rules.decision: Bind purchase identity to the correct account; grant once only after authoritative verification, then acknowledge through a recoverable path.
rules.trigger: A client success screen, pending payment or replayed token unlocks a paid feature.
rules.verification: Pending, wrong-account, repeated-purchase and acknowledgement-failure fixtures are covered.
rules.limits: Real purchase/refund/acknowledgement calls remain separate authorized actions.

rules.source_observation: Google Play RTDN signals a change but omits complete purchase state.
rules.decision: Authenticate the notification transport and fetch authoritative purchase state before updating entitlements.
rules.trigger: An RTDN type or timestamp is treated as the complete entitlement record.
rules.verification: Notification-only fixtures remain awaiting verification; API failure is recoverable without invented success.
rules.limits: Refreshing a subscription must remain possible after its purchase token has already been seen.

rules.source_observation: Planned sample demand depends on baseline, variance and detectable effect.
rules.decision: Check whether reachable eligible traffic can support the chosen effect size before launching an experiment.
rules.trigger: An A/B test is proposed for a very small audience.
rules.verification: Plan names assumptions, assignment unit, per-arm sample and acquisition constraints.
rules.limits: The bundled approximation is not exact power or a deadline guarantee.

rules.source_observation: Reaching a planned sample does not guarantee a significant result.
rules.decision: Predeclare the statistical engine and decision rule; report inconclusive rather than force a winner.
rules.trigger: A sample indicator or positive raw rate is treated as a win.
rules.verification: Readout retains interval/method, counts, uncertainty and stopping policy.
rules.limits: Do not use fixed-horizon significance with unrestricted repeated peeking; sequential engines need their own contract.

rules.source_observation: The research abstract identifies sample-ratio mismatch as a data-quality warning that can reverse decisions.
rules.decision: Resolve assignment/exposure integrity issues before interpreting uplift.
rules.trigger: Observed variant allocation materially conflicts with its configured allocation.
rules.verification: Investigate assignment, eligibility and event loss with an appropriate SRM test rather than assuming any numerical imbalance is a defect.
rules.limits: The abstract does not supply a universal SRM significance threshold.

rules.source_observation: Retention depends on entry/return definitions and reports incomplete periods separately.
rules.decision: Only compare mature, consistently defined cohorts; unknown future periods are not zero.
rules.trigger: Recent cohorts appear to collapse because their return window has not elapsed.
rules.verification: A cohort manifest names timezone, entry rule, return window and eligible denominator.
rules.limits: Day-N, on-or-after, rolling and subscription retention are not interchangeable.

rules.source_observation: Publisher metrics and product-retention views use distinct populations and aggregation choices.
rules.decision: Preserve metric grain, observation period and source class when joining evidence; never relabel benchmarks or fixtures as owner results.
rules.trigger: A small local rate is compared with an industry median or a weighted aggregate loses its denominator.
rules.verification: Every numeric row carries unit, statistic, population, window and provenance.
rules.limits: No business performance was measured in this research bundle.
